 UAE National Day 2026: Three-Day Break Announced – Will Schools Close Too?
 Eid Al Etihad 2026: A three-day public holiday has been announced for the UAE public sector. Will schools close too, and what about the private sector?
 Share 
 By Carli Allan
 The Report
 Local education top stories, summarised for you.
 Thank you for subscribing to our mailing list.
 First published: 13th Nov 2026
 Updated: 13th Nov 2026
 By Carli Allan
 The UAE has officially announced a three-day public holiday for federal government employees to celebrate the country's 55th National Day. But will private schools also close for three days, and when will the private sector holiday be confirmed?
 The Federal Authority for Government Human Resources (FAHR) announced on Friday, 13 November, that the Eid Al Etihad holiday for federal government employees will run from Wednesday, 2 December to Friday, 4 December 2026 , with official working hours resuming on Monday, 7 December.
 Combined with the Saturday and Sunday weekend, this means federal government employees will enjoy five consecutive days off.
 However, the official National Day holiday arrangements for private sector employees have not yet been announced.

 For parents across the UAE, the announcement also raises an important question: will their children's schools close for the same three days?
 Will UAE Schools Close for Three Days Over National Day 2026?
 The good news for parents is that the Ministry of Education's 2026–27 academic calendar already lists Wednesday, 2 December to Friday, 4 December as the National Day school holiday.
 However, while the three-day break has now been confirmed for federal government employees, an announcement from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) confirming the private sector holiday dates is still awaited.
 Eid Al Etihad, officially celebrated on 2 December each year, marks the founding of the United Arab Emirates in 1971. This year marks the country's 55th National Day.
 WhichSchoolAdvisor will update parents as soon as further announcements are made regarding private sector holidays and school closures.
